title: The zeta series is integral and rational
statement:
In the situation of [prop-rational-descent], the
point-count zeta series satisfies

$$
Z(X_0,T)\in1+T\mathbf Z[[T]]\cap\mathbf Q(T).
$$

proof.text: The hypotheses of [prop-rational-descent] give a proper scheme $X_0$ over $k_0=\mathbf F_q$. Proper means, in particular, of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Thus [prop-euler-product] applies with $Y_0=X_0$ and gives $Z(X_0,T)\in1+T\mathbf Z[[T]]$. Its series is the point-count exponential of [def-weil-point-counts-zeta], the same exponential used in the hypotheses; no change of zeta convention is involved.

source.place: Proof, first clause: the Euler-product integrality assertion, specialized to X_0

proof.text: Apply [prop-rational-descent] to the very same data and assumptions: the primes $p,\ell$, the finite field $k_0$, the smooth proper geometrically connected $X_0$ of pure dimension $d$, its cohomological family, the closed-point and trace-to-determinant identities, and the assumed finite Hankel rank over $\mathbf Q$. Every hypothesis is part of the situation in the statement of this item. Its conclusion is $Z(X_0,T)\in\mathbf Q(T)$.

source.place: Proof, second clause: by prop-rational-descent it also lies in Q(T)

proof.text: Steps 1 and 2 concern the same series $Z(X_0,T)$, so conjunction of their conclusions is exactly $Z(X_0,T)\in(1+T\mathbf Z[[T]])\cap\mathbf Q(T)$.

source.place: Proof, final sentence: This is the assertion.

proof_origin.place: Entire proof; expanded applications and intersection introduction

Step 1: X_0 is proper by def-weil-geometric-hypotheses, which means proper in the sense of def-weil-proper-morphism and so includes finite type. prop-euler-product's own statement says Z(Y_0,T) is in 1+TZ[[T]] for every finite-type F_q-scheme, so applying it to X_0 is a one-line specialization, and the zeta series is the same point-count exponential. Step 2 applies prop-rational-descent to the same data to get Z in Q(T). Step 3 combines the two conclusions. All three steps are genuinely elementary. On the route: prop-rational-descent is in the item's own unit; prop-euler-product's unit sk-prop-euler is cited by sk-thm-rationality; the other two cited nodes are definitions. No tool_uses, no SGA.
